Watch the interfaces move

Animated results for the poster An Explicit Multi-Time-Stepping Hybrid Scheme for the Allen–Cahn Equation, Kangwon National University.

Each clip shows a phase-field interface evolving under the Allen–Cahn equation. Parts of the interface with high curvature move faster, so sharp features smooth out first and closed interfaces shrink.

The model

The Allen–Cahn equation for the order parameter \(\phi\), with \(\phi=\pm1\) in the two phases:

\[ \frac{\partial \phi}{\partial t}=\Delta\phi-\frac{F'(\phi)}{\epsilon^{2}},\qquad F(\phi)=\tfrac{1}{4}\left(\phi^{2}-1\right)^{2} \]

The parameter \(\epsilon\) sets the thickness of the transition layer. As \(\epsilon\to0\), the interface moves by mean curvature, \(V=-\kappa\), so a circle of radius \(R\) shrinks as

\[ \frac{dR}{dt}=-\frac{1}{R},\qquad R(t)=\sqrt{R_0^{2}-2t}. \]
How HMTS computes one time step

The equation is split into diffusion and reaction. Diffusion is advanced with sub-steps \(\Delta t_k=\Delta t/2^{\,l-k}\), \(k=1,\dots,l\), starting from \(\phi^{*,0}=\phi^{n}\):

\[ \frac{\phi_i^{*,1}-\phi_i^{*,0}}{\Delta t_1}=\frac{\phi_{i-1}^{*,0}-2\phi_i^{*,0}+\phi_{i+1}^{*,0}}{h^{2}}, \] \[ \frac{\phi_i^{*,k}-\phi_i^{*,0}}{2\Delta t_{k-1}}=\frac{\phi_{i-1}^{*,k-1}-\left(\phi_i^{*,k}+\phi_i^{*,0}\right)+\phi_{i+1}^{*,k-1}}{h^{2}},\quad k=2,\dots,l. \]

The reaction is then solved exactly at each grid point:

\[ \phi_i^{n+1}=\frac{\phi_i^{*,l}}{\sqrt{e^{-2\Delta t/\epsilon^{2}}+\left(\phi_i^{*,l}\right)^{2}\left(1-e^{-2\Delta t/\epsilon^{2}}\right)}}. \]

Because the first level is explicit with \(\Delta t_1=\Delta t/2^{\,l-1}\), the scheme is stable for \(\Delta t/h^{2}\le 2^{\,l-1}/(2d)\).

S. Ahn, A. Raza and D. Jeong, “An explicit multi-time stepping hybrid scheme for the Allen–Cahn equation,” J. KSIAM 30(2) (2026), 339–358. doi.org/10.12941/jksiam.2026.30.339
